facts.text: Stowe was chartered on June 8, 1763, by Royal Governor Benning Wentworth of the Province of New Hampshire.
Stowe earned the nickname “The Ski Capital of the East” thanks to Stowe Mountain Resort’s terrain on Mount Mansfield, Vermont’s highest peak.
The Stowe Historical Society, founded in 1956 with help from the Vermont Historical Society, preserves the town’s past in two one‑room schoolhouses on School Street.
The Vermont Ski Museum, founded in 1988, moved to Stowe in 2000 and showcases the history of skiing and snowboarding in the state.
Stowe Land Trust, a local nonprofit started in 1987, has conserved 35 properties and more than 18 square kilometres of land for public use.
Stowe’s early economy relied on farming and lumber, with up to 8,000 sheep grazing the hills before the area shifted to dairy farms.
